news.title: Infantino’s World Cup sell-off debacle has rocked football but Fifa’s crisis has deep and rotten roots
news.lede: It has been a remarkable few days for an institution that may be irredeemable but this is a story that stretches back to a decision in 2010. There are decades in which nothing happens, and weeks in which decades happen, and those weeks tend to result in leaders being toppled. Not even a fortnight ago, Gianni Infantino was taking his victory lap on Instagram, attacking “those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours” who had dared to question elements of his World Cup, which had generated a record $15bn in revenues. But the next day came the revelation of his plan to sell the World Cup to outside investors and a backlash that has him scrabbling to save his presidency.

news.title: Gianni Infantino allies rally, as Norway FA demands FIFA president’s resignation
news.lede: Embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino visiting a sports complex in Cali, Colombia, on Aug 7. ZURICH - Football appeared to be headed for a prolonged standoff on Aug 7 as allies of FIFA president Gianni Infantino rallied behind him while Norway demanded his resignation after several European associations withdrew their support. Confederations and national associations continued to choose sides a week after Infantino abandoned his proposal to raise some US$4.2 billion (S$5.3 billion) by selling off a stake in the commercial rights of the World Cup and other tournaments. Norwegian Football Federation president Lise Klaveness said Infantino no longer had the confidence of the football community, saying the sport needed to move beyond “Game of Thrones” power struggles and focus on real governance reform.

news.title: Friends with tyrants, wants royal treatment & World Cup sale bid failed… so is Infantino now too toxic to run football?
news.lede: WELCOMING Fifa boss Gianni Infantino to the splendour of the Oval Office, Donald Trump anointed him the “king of soccer”. Once the target for childhood bullies, the football bureaucrat from humble beginnings was now being feted by the world’s most powerful man. It was likely a giant ego boost for someone not already lacking in that department — a TV contract at the 2022 World Cup stipulated that Infantino must be pictured onscreen at every game he attended. Yet, has the floundering Fifa chief’s puffed-up self-importance now chronically clouded his judgement?

news.title: Spain's Bernabéu 'preferred' for 2030 World Cup final ahead of Morocco's much larger 115,000-seat stadium
news.lede: The race to host the 2030 FIFA World Cup final appears to have taken another significant turn, with fresh reports suggesting Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabéu has moved into pole position to stage football's biggest match.
